Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

MosaiClusteR 1.0.0

First stable release. This version focuses on correctness: several functions that silently ignored an argument, mishandled an edge case, or failed to align multi-source inputs are fixed, and the documentation and vignette examples are corrected to match. Changes since 0.1.4:

Correctness fixes

  • Cluster() now forwards the normalisation method to Distance(). Previously the method argument was documented and accepted but silently ignored, and normalize = TRUE did not select a method. normalize now accepts either a logical (FALSE for none) or a normalisation method name, and method sets the method when normalize = TRUE.
  • Documentation examples now use the objects-in-rows orientation consistently (the Cluster() example no longer transposes the bundled mosaic_toy data).
  • cluster_agreement() edge cases. Identical partitions (up to relabelling) now return 1 for ARI, NMI and Jaccard, including the degenerate single-cluster and all-singleton cases that previously returned 0. Missing (NA) labels now raise a clear error instead of a cryptic “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”.
  • ADC() and ADEC() validate and align the sources by object identifier before combining them. Reordered rows are aligned to the first source; sources without row names are combined positionally (previously this failed with “need at least two non-NA values to interpolate”); and mismatched object sets, differing row counts or duplicated identifiers now raise clear errors instead of a cryptic “subscript out of bounds”.
  • mosaic_labels() validates k (a single positive integer) with a clear message, instead of silently truncating a non-integer k or failing cryptically on NA.
  • M_ABC() and ADEC() gained a seed argument for reproducible results, consistent with M_ABCdeep() and intNMF(). Their documentation states that they are stochastic and that seed (or set.seed()) fixes the result.
  • M_ABC() now aligns its sources by object identifier before building the consensus, so a source with reordered rows no longer changes the result; it also evaluates its List argument before seeding so an argument that uses the RNG cannot offset the internal random stream. CEC() uses the same alignment and now accepts sources without row names (combined positionally) instead of failing with “need at least two non-NA values to interpolate”.
  • Error messages for missing optional Bioconductor packages (used by the pathway and gene-set functions) now give the exact installation command, for example BiocManager::install("MLP"), instead of only “needed for this function to work”. The CRAN-package messages already named install.packages().

Documentation and examples

  • The vignette preprocessing example now computes distances from the normalised data, rather than normalising and then discarding the result.
  • The vignette method-comparison example reports each method’s name, success or failure status, runtime and a useful error message, instead of returning a bare NA on failure.
  • SelectnrClusters() returns one recommendation per criterion; the vignette now reduces these to a single validated integer before using it as a cluster count, rather than passing the whole table.
  • The five integration paradigms are stated consistently. Factor/low-rank and spectral methods (intNMF, spectral_clustering, LUCID) are presented as additional methods rather than a sixth paradigm.

MosaiClusteR 0.1.4

CRAN release: 2026-10-21

Third public release. It consolidates the development carried out after 0.1.1, which had not previously been published.

Breaking change

  • M_ABCpp() renamed to M_ABC(). The multi-source Aggregating Bundles of Clusters function is now M_ABC(); its arguments, behaviour and return value are unchanged. Update any calls from M_ABCpp(...) to M_ABC(...).

New features

  • The example dataset mosaic_toy is bundled in data/ and used by the examples and tests, so R CMD check (and the r-universe builds) no longer fail with “object ‘mosaic_toy’ not found”.
  • plot_pathways(style = "circular"). A radial (sunburst-style) bar plot that groups the enriched terms by cluster around a central hub. Bar length encodes p and colour encodes the cluster; each term is a single-line radial label that stays legible as the number of terms grows. Complements the existing "dotplot" and "lollipop" styles. It also gained cluster_cols (an explicit per-cluster palette, e.g. to match Cyclogram()) and wrap (radial label wrapping).
  • enriched_features(). A helper that turns CharacteristicFeatures() output into a per-cluster list of compact term/pvalue/Count tables, ready to hand straight to plot_pathways().
  • FeaturesOfCluster() and BinFeaturesPlot_SingleData() gained cexB, cexR and cexN arguments for the object, feature and name label sizes; Cyclogram() now defaults to a larger cex.labels.

Bug fixes

  • CharacteristicFeatures(). When called with binData (the common case, as in the documented example) an inner loop index overwrote the cluster index, so only the first cluster’s characteristic features were returned, and a datanames mis-index left the per-source result list unnamed. Both are fixed: features are now computed and named for every cluster.
  • Distance(distmeasure = "euclidean") now computes a true Euclidean distance (via stats::dist). Previously it routed to FD::gowdis (Gower), which returned NaN when a feature was constant across the selected objects, producing NA distance matrices. Gower is still available via distmeasure = "gower".
  • ComparePlot() (and Cyclogram()) now build a default colour palette when cols is not supplied, and check up front that all results describe the same objects, raising a clear message otherwise.

Metadata

  • The licence is GPL-3, consistent with 0.1.0 and 0.1.1. An interim local change to CC BY-SA 4.0 is reverted, since CC licences are intended for content rather than software.
  • “MoSaIC” expands to Multi-Omics Similarity Aggregation and Integrative Clustering in R, and the README framework overview is a scalable SVG figure (man/figures/framework.svg) that reads on both light and dark backgrounds.

MosaiClusteR 0.1.1

CRAN release: 2026-08-21

  • Documentation and installation updates to the README, and a package version bump from 0.1.0.

MosaiClusteR 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-07-29

First public release. MosaiClusteR is an umbrella framework for multi-source and multi-omics clustering: it gathers a broad catalogue of integration methods behind one consistent interface, together with the tooling needed to preprocess, select, evaluate, compare, characterise and biologically interpret the results.

Framework

  • Unified interface. Every method takes the same input — a List of numeric matrices over the same objects (objects in rows) — and returns the same {DistM, Clust} contract, so methods are interchangeable and directly comparable. Precomputed dissimilarities are accepted via type = "dist".
  • Four-layer workflow. Preprocess → baseline → integrate → evaluate.

Integration methods (five paradigms)

  • Direct: ADC(), ADEC().
  • Similarity-based: WeightedClust(), WonM(), SNF(), NEMO().
  • Graph-based: EnsembleClustering() (CSPA/HGPA/MCLA), HBGF(), ClusteringAggregation().
  • Voting / consensus: CEC(), CVAA(), ConsensusClustering(), EvidenceAccumulation(), LinkBasedClustering() (CTS/SRS/ASRS), and the Aggregating Bundles of Clusters family M_ABC() / M_ABCdist() / M_ABCdist.WC() / M_ABCdeep() (a deep-learning, autoencoder-based variant).
  • Hierarchy-based: HierarchicalEnsembleClustering(), EHC().
  • Factor / low-rank / spectral: intNMF(), spectral_clustering(), LUCID() (supervised, outcome-guided).
  • Cluster() provides the single-source baseline primitive.

Preprocessing, selection and evaluation

  • Preprocessing: Normalization() and Distance() (Euclidean, Manhattan, Tanimoto/Jaccard for binary data, correlation-based, and more).
  • Cluster-number selection: SelectnrClusters(), ChooseCluster().
  • Evaluation: mosaic_labels(), cluster_agreement() (ARI / NMI / Jaccard / purity), compare_clusterings(), CompareSilCluster(), CompareSvsM(), and data-driven source weighting (DetermineWeight_SilClust(), DetermineWeight_SimClust()).

Feature weighting and data nuggets

  • A data-nugget compression provides a robust, big-data-friendly feature weighting as an alternative to variance: create_data_nuggets(), nugget_feature_weights(), nugget_cluster(), Wkmeans(), Whclust().

Characterisation, visualisation and interpretation

  • Characterisation / navigation: CharacteristicFeatures(), FeatSelection(), FeaturesOfCluster(), FindCluster(), FindElement(), TrackCluster(), ReorderToReference(), SharedComps(), SimilarityMeasure().
  • Visualisation: ComparePlot(), ClusterPlot(), Cyclogram(), SimilarityHeatmap(), HeatmapPlot(), ProfilePlot(), ContFeaturesPlot(), BinFeaturesPlot_SingleData()/_MultipleData(), BoxPlotDistance(), and colour helpers (ColorPalette(), ColorsNames(), ClusterCols(), LabelCols()).
  • Biological interpretation (omics): DiffGenes(), PathwayAnalysis(), Pathways(), Geneset.intersect(), SharedGenesPathsFeat() and related functions connect clusters to genes and pathways.

Data and tests

  • Bundled mosaic_toy dataset and the mosaic_sim() structured-data generator.
  • A testthat suite covering distances, weighting schemes, the integration methods, evaluation metrics and data nuggets.

Notes

  • A compiled kernel (src/) accelerates the consensus step; building from source needs a C/C++ toolchain (Rtools on Windows). Heavier and specialised dependencies — SNFtool, circlize, plotrix, ggplot2, igraph, limma, MLP, biomaRt, org.Hs.eg.db and others — are declared under Suggests and loaded only when the corresponding method is called.
  • A few methods rely on an external graph-partitioning executable (e.g. METIS for EnsembleClustering(), the METIS path of EHC(), and LinkBasedClustering(linkBasedMethod = "asrs")) and raise an informative error when it is absent; pure-R alternatives (HBGF(), EvidenceAccumulation(), CTS/SRS) cover the same need.
